author: TheBeard
text:
HCDE wrote: Hi IF and team and everyone, I watched part 2 and i'm actually asking myself something which I'd like to submit to you for confirmation. What we see in part 2 are the best places (FL / KINKS) you tell us to wait for PA, but it doesn't mean that these are the only flags on a particular timeframe right? I mean it doesn't exempt us from finding other flags ect right? When i'm only marking those flags its rare for me to find PA... Hope this is clear...

FLs are everywhere. But not all are created equal, and not all a tradeable.

It's our job to find the ones that have the highest probability of getting a reaction.

So an FL that forms on the break of SR or at the left shoulder are more likely to get a reaction than one in the middle of nowhere. Although the IT's could use it at any time until it has proven itself not much we can do.

author: staurum
text:
I'm not sure if i understand the question. "What we see in part 2 are the best places (FL / KINKS) you tell us to wait for PA, but it doesn't mean that these are the only flags on a particular timeframe right?"

I interpret it as: FL/Kinks are places o wait for PA, but it doesn't mean these (FL/Kinks) are the only FLAGS on a particular timeframe?

Please do not misinterpret FL as Flag. Yes, FL can be a flag on a lower scale, but if we are talking on a particular, same scale, FL is the limit of a FLAG (a bigger one).

author: HCDE
text: Hi everyone, I'm still trying to work on those LS lines, and i have to admit that i haven't been able to make a comfortable use of what i've learned. There aren't many chart like USD CAD MN with a giant slide down, those are easy to mark, but on every other charts where you have many UP and downs, everything gets quickly very very subjective. I end up with an awful lot of lines. I did a lot of backtesting on what happens when price touches MPLs of kinks and i was astonished to see that in many case it bounces before or goes through easily. I 'm astonished because usually i can find good bounces on MPLs so i may not mark these kinks well. i'm more comfortable marking roughly my QM & Iqms than marking every LS on the chart. The problem with that is that sometimes price goes in my direction and falls down on an invisible hurdle and goes against me. Actually it happens really really often to me. That's why i tried to work out those LS kins of part 2 to make those hurdles visible. But with no success at the moment. I'm kind of desperate. So i'd like to know if any of you succeded in making a good use of the part 2?

author: Edge
text:
What seems to work for me is only using the best kinks to look for pa and using the other areas only as tgs.

In my view the true LS is the last push before the head and shift in direction ie the last trick. From a OF point you will see why
